_comment: Tighter-than-unconfined, NOT equivalent to Docker's own default profile. Docker's default is default-deny with a large explicit allowlist; that allowlist is generated from Go source at daemon startup and isn't available as a static file to diff against (see TODO.md), so this profile takes the opposite shape: default-ALLOW plus an explicit deny-list of syscalls a sandboxed or compromised Lean process has no legitimate reason to use. bubblewrap (apps/homework/sandbox.py) still needs the unshare/clone/mount family, which stays allowed here; Docker's own default profile is what blocks those and is why the compose files run with seccomp:unconfined today. Every entry below is denied with EPERM, verified against apps/homework/tests/test_sandbox.py running inside a container built with this profile in place of unconfined.

syscalls.comment: Process introspection/manipulation: lets a compromised process attach to and control sibling processes.
Kernel-level backdoors: no sandboxed process should ever load code into the kernel or eBPF VM.
Kernel keyring: no legitimate use inside a Lean sandbox, a known privilege-escalation surface.
